name: AD CS ESC1 — Subject Alt Name (SAN) Abuse
description: Abuse a certificate template with enrollee-supplied subject enabled (CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT) to request a certificate as any domain user including DA.

steps.label: Convert PEM to PFX (Linux)
steps.command: openssl pkcs12 -in cert.pem -keyfile key.pem -out cert.pfx -export -passout pass:<password>

examples.label: Convert cert to PFX
examples.command: openssl pkcs12 -in cert.pem -keyfile key.pem -out cert.pfx -export -passout pass:Password123

recommended.note: Enumerate the domain first to locate the CA and a vulnerable certificate template
DCSync with DA TGT obtained via cert
ESC3 as alternative enrollment agent path
Create golden ticket after krbtgt dump

notes: ESC1 conditions: Manager Approval=disabled, Auth. Signatures=0, EnhancedKeyUsage includes Client Authentication, enrollee supplies subject.

defense.why_it_works: AD CS (Active Directory Certificate Services) issues X.509 certificates used for Kerberos authentication (PKINIT). ESC1 occurs when a certificate template has: (1) Enrollee Supplies Subject = True (attacker specifies any Subject Alternative Name including another user's UPN), (2) Extended Key Usage includes Client Authentication, and (3) the template is accessible to low-priv users. The attacker enrolls for a certificate specifying a DA UPN as the SAN — the CA issues it. That certificate authenticates as the DA via PKINIT.
defense.prerequisites: Any domain user. Access to an AD CS CA. A vulnerable certificate template with CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT and Client Authentication EKU. Certify.exe or Certipy to find and exploit. Rubeus for PKINIT auth.
defense.impact: T1649 Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates + T1558 Kerberos Ticket Abuse. Obtains a certificate authenticating as any domain user (including DA/krbtgt). PKINIT produces a valid TGT for the impersonated account. Persistent — certificate valid for the template's lifetime (often 1 year). Survives DA password changes.
defense.detection:
Event 4887 (CA issued certificate): abnormal certificate requests where the SubjectAltName field contains a UPN different from the requesting user. MDI: 'Suspected AD CS ESC1 certificate request'. SIEM: CA audit log — certificate issued for user other than the requesting principal. Sysmon Event 25 (process tampering) if Certify.exe detected. CRL/OCSP analysis: certificate issued to non-matching principal.
Abnormal AD CS certificate enrollment and usage; registry access to certificate storage; unusual processes exporting or accessing private keys (DET0240/AN0671).
File access to certificate directories; OpenSSL or PKCS#12 utilities exporting/modifying certificates; processes accessing sensitive key storage paths (AN0672).
Keychain API calls and file access to ~/Library/Keychains or /Library/Keychains for stored certificates and private keys (AN0673).
Abnormal certificate enrollment in identity platforms; unexpected use of token-signing certificates; unusual CA configuration modifications (AN0674).
defense.artifacts: CA Event 4887: certificate issued with SAN different from requesting user | MDI: AD CS ESC1 alert | CA audit log: template with ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT used | Event 4768/4769: PKINIT logon using the fraudulent certificate
defense.prevention:
Disable 'Enrollee Supplies Subject' (CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT) on all templates that have Client Authentication EKU: Certificate Templates Console → Properties → Subject Name → uncheck 'Supply in the request'. Enable CA Manager Approval for any template that must keep this flag. Run Certify.exe /vulnerable regularly to audit templates. Deploy MDI. Restrict certificate template enrollment to specific groups.
Active Directory Configuration: Treat CA servers as tier-0 assets; harden abusable CA settings; disable SAN usage in authentication protocols to enforce strict user mappings; enforce CA Certificate Manager approval for templates with SAN issuance requirements.
Audit: Check and remediate unneeded certificates and common misconfigurations (enrollment permissions, overly permissive templates) via certsrv.msc, certutil.exe, PSPKIAudit, and Certify.
Disable or Remove Feature or Program: Disable old/dangerous auth protocols (NTLM) and unnecessary AD CS web/enrollment server roles.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Secure certificates and private keys; use TPM or HSM; enforce HTTPS and Extended Protection for Authentication.
defense.evasion: Request a certificate that matches a legitimate-looking user to avoid CA auditors noticing. Use the certificate over PKINIT for Kerberos (doesn't generate LDAP or SMB auth events). Combine with ESC3 for multi-step abuse that's harder to correlate.
defense.misconfiguration: Certificate template has CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT enabled AND Client Authentication EKU AND is enrollable by Domain Users. No CA Manager Approval. CA auditing not enabled.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Find vulnerable templates (Certify / Certipy):
Certify.exe find /vulnerable
# [!] Vulnerable Certificate Templates:
# Template: UserTemplate
# Enrollee Supplies Subject: True
# Extended Key Usages: Client Authentication
# Enrollment Permissions: Domain Users
# → ANY domain user can request cert as DA!

# CA has no Manager Approval:
# Certificate Templates → UserTemplate → Properties → Issuance Requirements
# → CA certificate manager approval: unchecked = auto-issue = VULNERABLE
defense.secure_config:
# Fix ESC1: disable 'Supply in the request':
# Certificate Templates MMC → right-click template → Properties
# → Subject Name tab → 'Supply in the request': UNCHECK
# → 'Build from Active Directory information': CHECK

# Or require CA Manager Approval:
# → Issuance Requirements → CA certificate manager approval: CHECK

# Audit vulnerable templates:
Certify.exe find /vulnerable
Certipy find -u user@corp.local -p pass -dc-ip 10.0.0.1 -vulnerable

# Enable CA audit logging:
# CA Properties → Auditing → Issue and manage certificate requests: CHECK
# Event 4887 will log all certificate issuances
